questions.question: Why is NeRF's density σ view-INDEPENDENT but color (r,g,b) is view-DEPENDENT?
options: Because physical matter doesn't disappear when you walk around it (density is fixed), but color changes with viewing angle due to specular reflections
Because the paper arbitrarily chose this design
questions.explanation: A rock has the same density from every angle — geometry is view-independent. But a shiny apple looks different from different angles (specular highlights). Separating them enforces physical correctness: geometry stays fixed, only appearance changes.

questions.question: What would happen if the MLP had NO non-linear activation functions (no ReLU)?
options: It would only represent linear functions (flat planes), because stacking linear operations is still linear
questions.explanation: Without non-linearity, the entire 8-layer network collapses to y = W·x + b (a single linear transformation). This can only represent flat planes — no curved surfaces, no complex geometry. ReLU is what gives neural networks their expressive power.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the skip connection at layer 4 in NeRF's MLP?
options: To help gradient flow during training and let the network 'remember' raw coordinates deep in the network
questions.explanation: After 4 layers of non-linear transformations, the raw coordinate information can be lost. The skip connection concatenates the original input with the layer-4 features, helping gradients flow and preserving positional information.
